title: Triplet Merge Target
statement:
Decide whether some of the given triplets can be merged, by taking position-wise maxima, into exactly a target triplet.

Contract
- `triplets` is a non-null array of arrays, each with exactly 3 ints (it may be empty); `target` has exactly 3 ints.
- You may choose any subset of the triplets (including just one). Merging them produces a triplet whose value at each position is the largest value found at that position among the chosen triplets.
- Return `true` if some non-empty subset merges into exactly `target`, otherwise `false`. An empty `triplets` array always gives `false`.
- Do not mutate the inputs.

Examples
- `canMerge(new int[][]{{2, 5, 3}, {1, 8, 4}, {1, 7, 5}}, new int[]{2, 7, 5})` returns `true` (merge the first and third; the middle one overshoots).
- `canMerge(new int[][]{{3, 4, 5}, {4, 5, 6}}, new int[]{3, 4, 5})` returns `true` using only the first triplet.
- `canMerge(new int[][]{{2, 3, 1}, {1, 2, 2}}, new int[]{2, 3, 3})` returns `false`.
hints: Merging can only raise values, so a triplet with any value above the target can never be part of a valid subset.
Among the remaining safe triplets, merging all of them is as good as any subset, since extra safe triplets cannot push a position past the target.
Scan once, ignore unsafe triplets, and record which of the three target positions is matched exactly by some safe triplet. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space for n triplets.
inputSyntax: Input: the triplets, a semicolon, then the target triplet, for example: [[2, 5, 3], [1, 8, 4], [1, 7, 5]]; [2, 7, 5]
